Below is a complete empirical plan tailored to the information provided and the constraints of the data.

1. Identification Strategy
- Primary strategy: First-difference IV (2SLS) using market-access changes as treatment and a pre-determined, least-cost-path network instrument.
  - We estimate the causal effect of reductions in trade costs between peripheral counties and large metropolitan nodes on changes in county outcomes between 1997 and 2006.
  - Treatment is the change in county-level market access to targeted metropolitan nodes caused by the rollout of NTHS. Because actual alignments and timing can be endogenous to growth prospects, we instrument ΔMA with a predicted change in access implied by an engineering least-cost network that connects the set of mandated NTHS nodes (provincial capitals, 1990 cities >500k, border crossings) using only pre-determined geographic costs (slope, rivers, etc.) and straight-line distances, constructed from 1990 cartography.
  - First-differences eliminate time-invariant county heterogeneity; instrument addresses endogenous placement and measurement error in ΔMA.
- Complementary robustness strategy: Within-corridor “geographic DiD”
  - Compare counties near vs. far from predicted corridors (e.g., within 0–20 km vs. 20–60 km bands) before/after, to generate a quasi-experimental contrast conditional on corridor fixed effects. This triangulates the IV results with a more local comparison.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable:
  - Main: ΔMA_i ≡ log(MA_i,2006) − log(MA_i,1997), where MA_i,t is a market-access index to targeted metropolitan nodes based on minimum travel times over the road/expressway network at time t. A standard measure is MA_i,t = Σ_j W_j / τ_ij,t, where j indexes targeted metros, W_j is the 1990 non-agricultural GDP (or population) of node j, and τ_ij,t is travel time from county i to j in year t. We will alternatively use an exponential decay MA_i,t = Σ_j W_j · exp(−κ · τ_ij,t), with κ chosen so that a 1-hour reduction is economically meaningful (e.g., κ ≈ 0.5–1).
  - Secondary binary exposure for robustness: Connected_i = 1 if county centroid lies within 10 km of an expressway segment completed by 2003 that links to at least one targeted metro with travel-time reduction ≥30% relative to 1997; 0 otherwise.
- Control group:
  - For IV: All peripheral counties not targeted as mandated nodes ex ante, with prefecture fixed effects, so identification is within-prefecture across counties that experienced different predicted access shocks.
  - For robustness within-corridor DiD: Counties 20–60 km from predicted least-cost corridors serve as controls for those 0–20 km, excluding any targeted nodes.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Baseline: 1997 (pre period); Post: 2006 (post period). Most NTHS mileage was built 1997–2003, with additional segments 2003–2007. Using 1997–2006 changes allows several years for adjustment while capturing the bulk of the program.
  - For the binary exposure, we use completion by 2003 to minimize post-2003 anticipatory/mid-construction confounding.
- Instrument:
  - ΔMA_hat_i computed from a least-cost-path network that connects mandated nodes using only 1990 geographic frictions (elevation/slope, rivers/coastline crossings, and fixed penalties for water crossings) and straight-line distances. Importantly, the instrument excludes contemporary or expected county-level economic variables. A “leave-province-out” variant (constructing least-cost paths holding out province-specific penalties) will be used to attenuate political influence on alignments.
  - We measure the predicted change between a “no-expressway” baseline and a “predicted expressway” network completed by 2003.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- For first-difference OLS component:
  - Parallel trends in absence of treatment (conditional on controls and prefecture FE): Treated and control peripheral counties within the same prefecture would have had similar 1997–2006 trend absent NTHS exposure. Plausibility: Within-prefecture comparisons reduce differential provincial policy shocks; we will probe with 1990–1997 placebo trends.
- For IV:
  - Relevance: The predicted least-cost network strongly correlates with actual access improvements to targeted metros (ΔMA_hat → ΔMA). Plausible given the program mandate to link specific nodes and engineering cost considerations.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on baseline controls and prefecture FE, the predicted least-cost access change affects outcomes only through realized access improvements (i.e., not through other concurrent policies targeted to the same predicted corridors). Plausible because instrument uses only 1990 geography and mandated nodes; we will bolster with controls for baseline transport (pre-1990 rail/roads), elevation/ruggedness, river proximity, and province-specific shocks.
  - Monotonicity: Counties predicted to have larger access gains under the least-cost network are weakly more likely to receive actual access improvements; no “defiers.” Reasonable under a nationwide trunk design with limited alternative alignments.
  - Stable unit treatment value: No interference beyond the channel captured by market access. Spatial spillovers are intrinsic to MA and are part of the estimand. Residual spillovers across nearby untreated counties could attenuate estimates; we will cluster SEs by corridor and test ring-exposure robustness.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- Endogenous route placement and timing within provinces:
  - Mitigation: Use IV with least-cost-path-based ΔMA_hat; include prefecture FE and baseline controls (1990 GDP levels and shares, population density, education, sectoral employment shares, distance to rivers/rail/ports, elevation/ruggedness). Add province-level time-varying controls (e.g., interaction of province dummies with a 1997–2006 indicator via first differences: province fixed effects in differences are absorbed by an intercept; we include Western Development Program province indicator).
  - “Leave-province-out” instrument and alternative cost surfaces (penalize river crossings differently) to show robustness of first stage and 2SLS.
- Confounding concurrent investments (e.g., rail expansions, industrial parks, WDP after 2000) correlated with predicted corridors:
  - Mitigation: Control for change in proximity to new rail lines or major ports (if available); include WDP province indicator; exclude counties with major seaport expansions as robustness; perform sub-sample excluding western provinces most affected by WDP.
- Differential pre-trends:
  - Mitigation: Placebo 1990–1997 growth on ΔMA (IV) must be null; include baseline trend controls: county-level 1990–1997 outcome growth as a control in main 2SLS; show balanced covariates by predicted exposure.
- Spatially correlated shocks and inference:
  - Mitigation: Cluster SEs by predicted corridor (or 200 km grid) to allow for spatial correlation; Conley (spatial-HAC) standard errors as robustness.

5. R Code Outline
Note: The code assumes pre-constructed CSVs with harmonized county panel, actual market access changes, and predicted instrument. Replace file paths as needed.

```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast OLS/IV with FE
library(sandwich)    # for vcovConley if desired
library(lmtest)

# 1) Data loading -----------------------------------------------------------
# counties.csv: one row per county with harmonized IDs and years
# Columns assumed:
# county_id, prefect_id, province_id, targeted_node (0/1),
# gdp_tot_1997, gdp_tot_2006, gva_ind_1997, gva_ind_2006,
# gva_serv_1997, gva_serv_2006, pop_1990, urban_pop_1997, urban_pop_2006,
# controls_1990_* (education90, popdens90, indshare90, agrishare90, servshare90, raildist90, riverdist, elevation, rugged),
# wdp_province (0/1), rail_change_97_06 (if available)

# ma_actual.csv: ΔMA_actual, log(MA_2006), log(MA_1997)
# ma_predicted.csv: ΔMA_hat (instrument), corridor_id (predicted corridor assignment), dist_to_pred_corridor_km

dt <- fread("data/counties.csv")
ma_a <- fread("data/ma_actual.csv")
ma_p <- fread("data/ma_predicted.csv")

# Merge
dt <- merge(dt, ma_a, by = "county_id", all.x = TRUE)
dt <- merge(dt, ma_p, by = "county_id", all.x = TRUE)

# 2) Variable construction --------------------------------------------------
# Outcomes: 1997-2006 log changes
dt[, d_gdp := log(gdp_tot_2006) - log(gdp_tot_1997)]
dt[, d_ind := log(gva_ind_2006 + 1) - log(gva_ind_1997 + 1)]
dt[, d_serv := log(gva_serv_2006 + 1) - log(gva_serv_1997 + 1)]
dt[, d_urban := (urban_pop_2006/pop_1990) - (urban_pop_1997/pop_1990)]  # if pop_1990 is stable denom; adjust per data

# Treatment and instrument
# ΔMA_actual and ΔMA_hat should be continuous. Ensure they are present.
stopifnot("dMA_actual" %in% names(dt), "dMA_hat" %in% names(dt))

# Binary exposure for robustness
dt[, connected2003 := as.integer(connected2003 == 1)]  # if provided; else create from highway completion data

# Controls (baseline 1990)
ctrls <- c("education90","popdens90","indshare90","agrishare90","servshare90",
           "raildist90","riverdist","elevation","rugged","wdp_province","rail_change_97_06")

# Sample: peripheral counties only (exclude mandated nodes)
dt_periph <- dt[targeted_node == 0 & !is.na(d_gdp) & !is.na(dMA_actual) & !is.na(dMA_hat)]

# 3) Main specification: 2SLS in first differences --------------------------
# Regress change in outcomes 1997–2006 on change in market access (instrumented)
# Prefecture fixed effects; weight by 1990 population (optional)
wts <- dt_periph$pop_1990
form_iv <- as.formula(paste0(
  "d_gdp ~ ", paste(ctrls, collapse = " + "),
  " | prefect_id | dMA_actual ~ dMA_hat | corridor_id"
))

# IV with prefecture FE and clustering by predicted corridor
est_iv <- feols(form_iv, data = dt_periph, weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
summary(est_iv)
etable(est_iv, se = "cluster")

# First-stage diagnostic
fs <- fitstat(est_iv, type = "ivf")  # Kleibergen-Paap F if available; else look at first stage in summary

# Alternative outcomes
est_iv_ind  <- feols(update(form_iv, d_ind  ~ .), data = dt_periph, weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
est_iv_serv <- feols(update(form_iv, d_serv ~ .), data = dt_periph, weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
est_iv_urb  <- feols(update(form_iv, d_urban~ .), data = dt_periph, weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)

# 4) Robustness checks ------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Placebo pre-trend: 1990–1997 growth on instrumented ΔMA
# Require 1990 levels; construct d_gdp_90_97 if available
if(all(c("gdp_tot_1990","gva_ind_1990","gva_serv_1990") %in% names(dt_periph))){
  dt_periph[, d_gdp_90_97 := log(gdp_tot_1997) - log(gdp_tot_1990)]
  form_iv_placebo <- as.formula(paste0(
    "d_gdp_90_97 ~ ", paste(ctrls, collapse = " + "),
    " | prefect_id | dMA_actual ~ dMA_hat | corridor_id"
  ))
  est_placebo <- feols(form_iv_placebo, data = dt_periph, weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
  summary(est_placebo)
}

# (b) Near–far around predicted corridors (geographic DiD-style)
# Define bands
near_band <- 20; far_min <- 20; far_max <- 60
dt_band <- dt_periph[dist_to_pred_corridor_km <= far_max]
dt_band[, near := as.integer(dist_to_pred_corridor_km <= near_band)]
# Simple OLS in first differences within-corridor, with corridor FE
est_band <- feols(d_gdp ~ near + near:wdp_province + connected2003 + 
                    education90+popdens90+indshare90+agrishare90+servshare90+
                    raildist90+riverdist+elevation+rugged | corridor_id,
                  data = dt_band[dist_to_pred_corridor_km >= far_min], 
                  weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
summary(est_band)

# (c) Exclude Western Development Program provinces
est_iv_nowdp <- feols(form_iv, data = dt_periph[wdp_province == 0], weights = ~pop_1990, cluster = ~corridor_id)
summary(est_iv_nowdp)

# (d) Conley spatial-HAC SEs (optional if coordinates are available)
# if "lon","lat" exist:
# vc <- vcov_conley(est_iv, lat = ~lat, lon = ~lon, cutoff = 200000)  # 200 km
# coeftest(est_iv, vcov. = vc)
```

6. Expected Results
- Theory suggests ambiguity: at intermediate trade costs, agglomeration forces can pull manufacturing toward cores; at very low trade costs, dispersion can occur if wage or land-rent differentials dominate. Given China’s strong urban agglomerations in the 1990s and the program’s core-connecting objective:
  - Total GDP in peripheral counties: modest positive elasticity with respect to market access (diffusion of non-tradables and some tradables). Prior: 10% increase in MA raises county GDP by about 1–2%.
  - Industrial GVA: weaker and possibly zero or negative average effect in small peripheral counties if manufacturing concentrates in metros. Prior: elasticity between −0.2% and +0.5% per 10% MA increase, heterogeneous by initial industrial base.
  - Services GVA and urbanization: positive; services and construction respond locally. Prior: elasticity 1–2% per 10% MA increase for services; urbanization rate increases by 0.3–0.8 percentage points for a one standard deviation increase in ΔMA.
  - Heterogeneity: counties that were already semi-industrial in 1990 likely benefit more on industrial outcomes; purely agricultural counties may see services and commuting growth rather than local industry.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
- C1: Strong instrument relevance (first-stage F-stat > 10 within prefecture, corridor clustering). Score: 1 if achieved; anticipate 1 given the mandate and geography.
- C2: Exclusion restriction plausible after controls (instrument uses only 1990 geography and mandated nodes; control for baseline transport/topography and province shocks). Score: 0.5–1 (some residual concern about correlated investments along natural corridors).
- C3: No differential pre-trends (placebo 1990–1997 growth vs. instrumented ΔMA shows null). Score: 1 if placebo passes; otherwise 0.
- C4: Stable sample/consistent boundaries and no endogenous selection into “peripheral” sample. Harmonized county units are used; targeted nodes excluded. Score: 1.
- C5: Robustness across specifications (alternative MA functional forms, near–far bands, excluding WDP provinces, alternative cost surfaces). Score: 1 if results persist qualitatively.

Notes on implementation and measurement
- Market access construction: Use targeted metros’ 1990 non-agricultural GDP or population as weights; compute minimum travel times with (i) pre-1997 network, (ii) 2006 network. If only expressways are digitized, include pre-existing primary roads via fixed speed assumptions or treat 1997 MA as baseline from non-expressway network and add expressways in 2006.
- Instrument construction: Build least-cost paths on a raster cost surface using elevation-derived slope and water-crossing penalties calibrated from engineering sources; connect all mandated nodes in a Steiner-tree-like network and derive county-level ΔMA_hat. A “leave-province-out” variant recalculates paths excluding within-province pairwise links to reduce province-level discretion biases.
- Inference: Cluster by predicted corridor (or 200 km grid). Report Conley SEs as sensitivity.
- Spillovers: Because MA aggregates over nodes, general-equilibrium spillovers are part of the estimand. As a check, re-estimate excluding counties within 50 km of targeted metros to focus on truly peripheral exposure.
